The generic name is conserved, and the type species of Fabronia is F. pusilla (Wijk et al., 1960;(Index of Moss Names, 2024). The genus is recognized by its usually complanate, feathery shoots and ovate to lanceolate leaves with well-defined, single costae and toothed to entire margins, often bearing papillae or short basal prorulae. The perichaetial leaves are typically differentiated, and the double peristome bears 16 more or less equal exostome teeth and a weakly developed endostome with short or vestigial segments; capsules are inclined to horizontal and usually smooth (Buck and Ireland, 1989; Allen, 2002). Ovary/placentation are referable to the standard pleurocarpous pattern, and the capsule dehisces by an operculum, with elater-like structures frequently absent in Fabronia (Buck and Ireland, 1989). Diversity peaks in the Neotropics and in tropical Asia, with several regionally endemic species, including narrow Island endemics in the Pacific and New Caledonia. Habitats are typically epiphytic on trunks and branches in lowland to montane humid forests, sometimes extending into limestone or serpentine outcrops.
